layer5_verifier_fairness_static.explanation: All mandatory verifier subchecks pass. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__require.explanation: Each verifier carries a requirement_id and evidence_span that maps to instruction text (R1_* -> the register spec, R2_* -> the summary spec, R3_* -> the column X recording clause). layer5_verifier_fairness_static__coverag.explanation: Grading is field level, not existence level: register_population locks the population as a multiset keyed on MRN plus rows_after_table == 0; the four group checks assert Dose, Result and Days late per MRN; the summary checks assert each label's value, absence of hedged alternatives and cross-occurrence consistency, plus page and character caps; the column_x checks assert the exact wording per row index and nothing_else_recorded is a recall-gated precision lock. An empty or missing deliverable fails every relevant check (a missing PDF fails the in_array value assertion and the extent checks even though the vacuous 'alternatives == []' sub-assertion would hold, because pass_threshold is 1.0 over all sub-verifiers).

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__evidenc.explanation: Artifact requirements are read from the artifacts (xlsx.read_rows on sheet 'Audit', pdf.find_labeled_value/inspect_document on the summary) at the agent's workspace; connector-state requirements are read from the gym DB over the trusted socket with the correct spreadsheet_id/sheet_id/column_index 23. No check substitutes trajectory data for an artifact requirement or vice versa, and _spec_paths_under_input blocks any spec that would grade a seeded input.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__semanti.explanation: Equivalent renderings survive: table_equals normalises text by strip/casefold/whitespace-collapse, parses numbers (so 0 vs '0' vs '0.00' match within 1e-3), keys rows through id_pattern so '8520-2125' matches regardless of surrounding punctuation, imposes no column order, no extra-column lock and no row order; find_labeled_value accepts an optional separator, is case-insensitive, allows up to two extra label words, tolerates line wrap and varied spacing, and parses grouped/scaled numbers. Column X is compared with lower(trim(...)), so capitalisation and padding do not matter.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__surface.explanation: Every matcher was inspected. id_pattern ^\W*([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4})\W*$ accepts the MRN with surrounding punctuation; SQL uses lower(trim(coalesce(value_text,''))) = lower('<result>'), so only the protocol-mandated wording (explicitly required by the instruction) is enforced and case/whitespace variation passes; the PDF label regex is unanchored and wrap-tolerant. Nothing can be passed by mimicking tokens: the summary values must equal the correct integers, the register must carry the right per-MRN triple, and the column X checks are gated on no other row being written, so copying a result word into every row fails three of the four group checks.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__verifie.explanation: All 15 configs are executed by run_benchmark_verifiers; none is skipped or silently dropped (an unsupported type would be marked unscored and would force failure_mode=verifier_error). Infrastructure failures are surfaced rather than hidden: _emit_engine_owned_reward raises instead of writing a score when the engine reports verifier_error, run_verifier isolates a per-verifier infrastructure error onto that row, and test.sh propagates the non-zero exit without manufacturing a reward.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__score_b.explanation: Only one bucket is represented as active - the engine ('rubric' weight 1.0) - and it holds all 15 weighted items. state (expected_diff.json = {}), sql and trajectory carry weight 0.0 and are excluded from allowed_verifier_types, so no empty or unreachable bucket is presented as coverage. rubric.toml contributes zero rubric_check items, which is consistent with weights summing to 1.0 across the 15 authored verifiers alone.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__aggrega.explanation: scoring.flat_verifier_scoring = true, so run_benchmark_verifiers computes sum(passed weight)/sum(weight) over the items; the authored weights sum to exactly 1.0 (0.07+0.10+0.09+0.09+0.05+0.05x4+0.03+0.09+0.08+0.08+0.05+0.07). Recomputing: a perfect run = 1.0 and pass=true (core_passed requires every item to pass); losing only register_given_late yields 0.91 with pass=false; losing a stray column-X write trips the shared guard in all four column_x checks and nothing_else_recorded, yielding 0.63. Declared weights therefore equal the effective reward math, and the per-type averaging path is bypassed.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__scoring.explanation: Weight tracks materiality: the register population lock 0.07, the four result groups 0.33 in proportion to their sizes (9/4/5/1 rows -> 0.10/0.09/0.09/0.05), the four summary totals 0.20, the column X write-back 0.37, and the purely formal extent bound only 0.03. No fatal omission is masked - a missing deliverable zeroes every check that reads it - and pass/fail is all-or-nothing (core_passed), so partial credit only shapes the continuous reward.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__check_i.explanation: The register population lock lives only in register_population (the group checks deliberately omit row_set), each group check reads a disjoint set of MRNs, and the PDF totals are independent labels. The one shared predicate is the 'no other row written in column X' guard embedded in all four column_x checks plus nothing_else_recorded; that coupling is explicitly disclosed in each check's metadata as a hedge guard, and its purpose (refusing a shotgun write that would otherwise collect group credit) justifies the overlap.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__counter.explanation: Positive: the oracle's artifacts satisfy every assertion. Negative: wrong grouping of any client fails the group check that names her and the corresponding summary total. Incomplete: a missing register row fails register_population; a missing PDF fails all five summary checks. Adversarial: a shotgun 'Given on time' across all clients trips the hedge guard; writing results for the Rh-positive distractor or older pregnancies loses nothing_else_recorded and all four column_x checks; a hedged PDF line ('9 or 10') is caught by $.alternatives == []; dumping the register into the PDF is caught by the page/char caps. consistency/mutations.json records the same battery over the 10 file_check verifiers with 100% strictness and 0% brittleness.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static.explanation: All mandatory verifier subchecks pass. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__require.explanation: consistency/requirements.json maps one row per requirement_id in tests/manifest.json to a verbatim instruction span and names the grading verifier; I checked each span against instruction.md and the procedure. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__coverag.explanation: Checks are field-level, not existence-level. register_changes uses table_equals with a 51-id row_set lock plus a per-row Change value; register_dropped locks the two export-form ids as a set; each Summary metric is asserted as a typed number and summary_metric_rows locks the metric population to exactly six. On the connector side, 13 row checks assert the label text AND the co-located instance id in column D, and nothing_else_recorded_or_changed only pays when all 51 row labels match, then requires zero other non-empty cells in column Y or right of it, exact cell counts/char-length/number-sum for the rest of the workbook, an exact cell count for every other spreadsheet and exactly 7 sheets. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__evidenc.explanation: Artifact requirements are read from the artifact: file_check verifiers run xlsx.read_rows on run_changes.xlsx in the agent workspace (the engine even refuses specs that point at seeded input files). layer5_verifier_fairness_static__semanti.explanation: Tested the plausible variants against compare.py. Column names match after strip, quote-stripping and casefold; text cells (including both id columns, which declare cell_types 'text') match after strip + casefold + whitespace-run collapse, so 'newly passing', 'Newly  Passing' and trailing spaces all pass. Summary values are typed 'number' with tolerance 0.005 and parse_cell_number accepts 51, '51', 51.0, '51.00', '$51', '1,200'-style grouping — mutations.json confirms 'every integer written as a float' scores 9/9. The Summary id_pattern strips leading/trailing whitespace, asterisks, underscores, colons, periods and hyphens, so '**Newly passing:**' still keys. Row order is not locked (no row_set_ordered), extra sheets and extra columns are tolerated. The forms that are required (label strings, metric names, sheet/header names, the two id renderings) are each explicitly prescribed by the instruction or the procedure.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__surface.explanation: Every matcher was inspected. The SQL cell comparisons use lower(trim(coalesce(value_text,''))) = lower('<label>'), tolerant of case and surrounding whitespace. The only regex used for grading is the Summary id_pattern '^[\s*_:\-]*(.*?)[\s*_:.\-]*$', which strips markdown/punctuation decoration from the metric label and leaves the semantic text intact. There is no SQL LIKE/REPLACE on agent text and no token whitelist. A wrong answer cannot pass by mimicking tokens: row_set locks make supersets and subsets fail (mutations.json: 'correct answer PLUS one extra row' fails on each sheet), the summary values are numbers, and nothing_else_recorded_or_changed is gated on all 51 labels being positionally correct. Each matcher checks at least what its description claims.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__verifie.explanation: Entrypoint chain test.sh -> test_gvs.sh -> /app/tests/test_outputs.py traced; run_benchmark_verifiers dispatches file_check and database_state through the vendored VerifierEngine, and an unknown type would be marked unscored (making the run ungradable) rather than silently skipped. evaluations/oracle/verifier/{test-stdout.txt,verifier_summary.json} show all 24 items executed with error null, unscored 0, failed 0. Infrastructure failures are not laundered into scores: _emit_engine_owned_reward raises instead of emitting a reward when the engine reports an error or failure_mode 'verifier_error', leaving the trial unscored.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__score_b.explanation: All 24 buckets carry a non-zero weight and all 24 received evidence in the checked-in oracle run. The state, sql and trajectory axes are declared at weight 0.0 and excluded from allowed_verifier_types, i.e. explicitly inactive rather than presented as coverage; their artefacts (solution/expected_diff.json = {}, empty snapshots) are consistent with that. tests/rubric.toml has no criteria, so zero rubric_check items are synthesised — the 'rubric' weight of 1.0 is just the axis label under which the engine's own weighted score is reported, as _emit_engine_owned_reward documents.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__aggrega.explanation: Recomputed. scoring.flat_verifier_scoring = true pools every item by weight: 0.19 + 0.06 + 6x0.04 + 0.02 + 14x0.025 + 0.14 = 1.000. All passing gives 1.0, matching evaluations/oracle (reward.txt 1.0, reward.json {"reward": 1.0}, verifier_summary total/composite 1.0). Representative partials: failing only summary_regressed -> 0.96; failing only nothing_else_recorded_or_changed -> 0.86; failing register_changes plus its three re-run-sensitive Summary rows (the documented default misreading) -> 1 - 0.19 - 0.04 - 0.04 - 0.14 = 0.63. No hidden gate alters this: the side-effect hard gate is a state-axis concept and the engine path reports side_effect_gate 1.0 with state disabled; 'pass' is the engine's core-based overall_success, while the scalar reward is the weighted score.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__scoring.explanation: Weight tracks materiality: the 51-row per-instance register is the heaviest single check (0.19), the connector-side write-back totals 0.485 across 13 row checks plus the 0.14 full-recall/precision lock, the six requested Summary metrics get 0.04 each, and the pure layout lock (summary_metric_rows) gets only 0.02. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__check_i.explanation: Overlap exists but is disclosed and justified. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__counter.explanation: consistency/mutations.json records 23 cases run through this bundle's own engine against the gold workspace: positive (9/9 file_checks pass), semantic (each corrupted Summary value fails exactly its own verifier), granularity (one corruption fails exactly one verifier), cosmetic (extra sheet, extra column, floats written for integers all still 9/9), incompleteness (dropping the last data row of each sheet fails the owning verifier), and adversarial acceptance (a superset row on each sheet fails; every figure off by one fails all six value checks). layer5_verifier_fairness_static__semanti.explanation: The comparators are normalising. table_equals grades 'Instance id' and 'Decision' under the 'text' type (strip + casefold + collapsed whitespace) and headers via normalize_header (strip, unquote, casefold), so 'accept' / 'Accept ' / 'DECISION' all survive; Instances/Accepted are typed 'number' so 10, '10', '10.0' and ' 10 ' all parse. The labeled_value grammar tolerates currency, grouping, hedging detection and up to two extra words plus a bracketed unit after the stem. The SQL equality is case- and whitespace-insensitive. Token mimicry cannot pass: copying 'Accept' into every G cell fails 43 of the 51 correlated row checks and the exclusivity gate. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__score_b.explanation: The only active bucket is the engine's pooled verifier list, and it holds all 58 weighted checks. scoring.weights sets sql=0.0, state=0.0, trajectory=0.0 and allowed_verifier_types excludes them, and the emitted reward.json records state.enabled=false / sql.enabled=false with score null — so no empty or zero-weight bucket is represented as coverage. layer5_verifier_fairness_static__aggrega.explanation: With scoring.flat_verifier_scoring = true, run_benchmark_verifiers computes Σ(weight·passed)/Σ(weight) over all scored items. Cosmetic differences (fonts, runs, extra sheets/columns, float formatting) cost nothing — confirmed by the 'cosmetic' mutation cases. A fatal omission is not masked: do-nothing fails all 14 file checks and all 5 DB checks. The single stray column-W write that zeroes all five database_state checks (0.34) is a large but defensible penalty, since 'Record nothing for any other client' is a privacy requirement and hedge-all is the primary cheap exploit.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__check_i.explanation: The 14 file checks are mutually independent: the mutation battery shows one corrupted value fails exactly the verifier that grades it (controls 'semantic' and 'granularity', 1 failing verifier each). The five database_state checks deliberately share two predicates — the untouched-row guard zeroes all four group checks, and nothing_else_recorded returns -1 unless all 65 rows are already correct. That coupling is disclosed on the face of the configs (description 'Once every touched record carries its action, no other row has a value in column W'; why_justification 'hedge-all guard' / 'recall-gated precision lock'), so the overlap is stated rather than hidden, and it is the mechanism that makes the hedge-all exploit unprofitable.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__counter.explanation: consistency/mutations.json records a run of the bundle's own specs through the vendored engine with concrete positive, semantic, granularity, cosmetic, incompleteness and adversarial cases: the oracle artifacts score 14/14; dropping a row fails population plus its group; an extra row fails the population lock; every figure off by one fails all six Summary checks; +5/+10/+20 invented rows, one-row-names-everything, swapped actions, hedge-all-premature, the lazy 'released holds still protect' reading, a missing 7687-2951, and do-nothing all lose; while correct alternative renderings (xlsxwriter real dates, hand-built OOXML, To/From table first, reordered rows, alternative date and case spellings, a title row above each header) all score 1.0. strictness 100%, brittleness 0%, superset_report_accepted=false. The column-W side is covered structurally: the group counts and the exclusion-list guard distinguish the lazy, hedging and partial readings named in the gold metadata.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__process.explanation: Reward depends solely on outcomes — the two deliverable files and the connector's column W. trajectory weight is 0.0, forbidden_tools is empty, there is no trace rubric, and no check inspects tool names, call counts or narration. The harness-specific trajectory file is used only for evidence display, not scoring.

layer5_llm_judge_design.explanation: No LLM judge grades anything in this task. tests/rubric.toml contains only a [system] preamble with no [[criteria]], so _rubric_check_verifiers_from_rubric yields zero verifiers, and all 19 manifest.verifier_configs are file_check or database_state — none routes to _run_rubric_check or _run_response_check. metadata.verifier_judge exists only as a precondition gate: score_benchmark_verifiers returns an error block if the model id or OPENAI_API_KEY is absent, and _emit_engine_owned_reward then raises so the run is recorded UNSCORED rather than zero.

layer5_llm_judge_design__judge_execution.explanation: No judge call is ever issued: zero rubric_check/response_check verifiers exist, so the configured model (${JUDGE_MODEL:-openai/zai-org/GLM-5.2}) and OPENAI_API_KEY are never used to produce a score.

layer5_llm_judge_design__judge_failure_h.explanation: No judge is invoked. layer5_llm_judge_design__judge_context_c.explanation: There are no rubric questions, so no judge prompt or attachment set exists to assess.

layer5_llm_judge_design__repeat_stabilit.explanation: Scoring is fully deterministic (typed table comparison plus SQL equality), so there is no judge variance to control.

layer5_reward_hacking_static.explanation: All four exploitability subchecks pass: no shortcut passes without actually producing the correct 65-row classification in both deliverables and in column W, the answer key is unreadable, the connector is reachable only through the sanctioned MCP tool, and grading state is root-owned.

layer5_reward_hacking_static__rollout_le.explanation: Grading is final-surface only, but the final surface is hard to fake: the Actions sheet must carry the exact 65-MRN population with per-row last-activity dates and actions, the Summary the six exact figures, the notice exactly the three premature MRNs with both dates, and the live connector sheet exactly 65 correctly-worded W cells and no others. A fabricated or looping rollout that does not actually derive the classification cannot produce that state. Destructive behaviour elsewhere in the sheet is not penalised (the state axis is off), which is the one legitimacy gap, and it cannot earn reward.

layer5_reward_hacking_static__sanctioned.explanation: The agent's only connector path is the public proxy's /mcp/gws-gym mount exposing the single `gws` tool. The raw control plane (/raw/{name}/state, /raw/{name}/step, /seal-tool-trace) is bound exclusively to the root-owned unix socket and additionally requires the per-run verifier capability from a 040 root:harborproxy file. entrypoint.sh locks /gyms to 710 root:gym and chmods connector state go-rwx, and preflight_connector_boundary refuses to start unless the gym rejects a bare direct /step, so bypassing the proxy over localhost is blocked.

layer5_reward_hacking_static__golden_or_.explanation: tests/manifest.json (which lists every expected MRN, date and count) and task.toml (whose metadata.scenario_description spells out the gold) live under /app, which the Dockerfile makes 0700 root via `chmod -R go-rwx /app` while the agent runs as rlgymagent. solution/ is never copied into the image. The agent-visible fixtures are only the two legitimate inputs under /workspace/provided.

layer5_reward_hacking_static__state_spoo.explanation: Reward-bearing state is not agent-writable: the column-W facts are read from the connector DB through the root-only socket, not from any agent-supplied file; /logs/verifier is created root:root 0700 before the agent exists, with an explicit guard refusing a pre-existing symlink or non-directory, and /logs itself is verified as 0:0:755. layer1_package_consistency.explanation: task.toml, instruction.md, solution/*, tests/*, environment/* and the environment/_app mirror describe one executable, gradable task. instruction_sha256 in tests/manifest.json (242174b7...) matches sha256(instruction.md); `diff -r tests environment/_app/tests`, task.toml and instruction.md mirrors are byte-identical; the Dockerfile FROM digest equals metadata.mcp_servers_extended image digest (sha256:eac5acca...); deliverable paths (/workspace/performance_triage.xlsx, /workspace/regression_summary.pdf) match the file_check arguments and the Dockerfile WORKDIR /workspace. layer1_package_consistency__cross_artifa.explanation: No source is missing. instruction.md names both provided inputs, which exist at environment/provided/benchmark_baselines.csv (29 register rows, 2 'not yet benchmarked') and environment/provided/performance_regression_policy.docx (scope, tolerances, Regression/Within tolerance/No baseline wording) and are COPYed to /workspace/provided and /app/provided. solution/ (solve.sh, solve.py, golden_trajectory.json 49 steps, artifact_plan.json, write_artifacts.py, final_answer.md) and tests/ (test.sh -> test_gvs.sh -> test_outputs.py + manifest.json with 27 verifier_configs) jointly define the task, its gold and its scoring.

layer1_package_consistency__instruction_.explanation: Every reward-bearing check traces to instruction text: REQ-PR-REG (reports_register) -> 'a sheet named Reports with the header row Issue | ... | Result and one row per report the policy covers ... nothing underneath'; REQ-PR-PDF-1/2 -> 'one line per repository that has at least one Regression' and 'one page'; REQ-PR-TOT-1/2 -> the three reserved total labels quoted verbatim in the instruction; REQ-PR-FLAG-1/2 -> 'one new issue per regression ... titled exactly `Performance regression: owner/name#N`'; REQ-PR-ONLY (nothing_written_beyond_the_regression_log) -> 'Open no other issue, and write nothing else on GitHub'. consistency/requirements.json carries a verbatim prompt_span per requirement_id. layer1_package_consistency__solution_ver.explanation: evaluations/oracle/verifier/verifier_summary.json shows all 27 verifier_configs executed and passed (verification_summary total 27, passed 27, weighted_pass_rate 1.0; file_check 1.0, database_state 1.0) and evaluations/oracle/verifier/reward.txt is 1.0. solve.sh explicitly stages the oracle's deliverables into ${TH_WORKSPACE_DIR:-/workspace} so the file_check verifiers find them (evaluations/oracle/agent/oracle.txt logs performance_triage.xlsx and regression_summary.pdf written into /workspace). layer1_clarity_scope.explanation: Fails because the mandatory subcheck layer1_clarity_scope__representation_contract fails: the PDF repository lines are graded by regexes that silently require the two counts to follow the repository name separated only by whitespace/punctuation, a representation choice the instruction never states. The other three subchecks (output surface, process disclosure, redaction readability) pass, but general clarity does not compensate for an undisclosed formatting requirement that can cost 18% of reward.

layer1_clarity_scope__output_surface_con.explanation: The verifier grades exactly the three surfaces the instruction names: the xlsx and pdf in /workspace (six file_check verifiers) and GitHub side effects in susanthomas/d3-charts plus the register repositories (21 database_state verifiers). Nothing grades the chat response: in engine mode the evidence block's final_output/agent_messages are only consumed by rubric_check/response_check verifiers, of which this task declares none (tests/rubric.toml has only a [system] preamble). No connector state outside the instruction's scope is rewarded.

layer1_clarity_scope__representation_con.explanation: The PDF repository lines carry an undisclosed representation requirement. Each of the 15 row_* checks in summary_repository_lines (and repository_row_population) matches '<owner/name>[\s|,;:/·•\-–—]+<covered>[same class]+<regressions>', i.e. the separator class admits only whitespace and punctuation — never words. I tested the gold pattern for GitLab/eco-tracker: 'GitLab/eco-tracker | 2 | 1', '... 2 1', '..., 2, 1' and '... — 2 — 1' all match, but 'GitLab/eco-tracker: 2 covered, 1 regression', 'GitLab/eco-tracker - 2 reports covered, 1 regression' and 'GitLab/eco-tracker (2 covered, 1 regression)' all fail. instruction.md only says the line gives 'its owner/name, how many open performance reports the policy covers there and how many of them are Regressions, in that order' — it prescribes order, never bare unlabelled numerals, and it explicitly prescribes labels for the three totals, which makes a labelled repository line a natural reading. layer1_clarity_scope__process_requiremen.explanation: No reward depends on narration, a particular tool, or a prescribed workflow. The 27 scored verifiers read only deliverable files and post-run DB state; manifest.trajectory has weight 0 in scoring.weights and no trajectory verifier is declared. layer1_clarity_scope__redaction_readabil.explanation: instruction.md contains no placeholders, elisions or broken grammar. layer1_realism_leakage.explanation: All four mandatory subchecks pass: the policy arithmetic is correct and self-consistent, the supplied authorities are valid and applicable, the workflow is a plausible performance-triage task, and the golden/answer material is unreachable from the agent's identity and filesystem.

layer1_realism_leakage__domain_correctne.explanation: I recomputed every one of the 44 classifications from environment/provided/benchmark_baselines.csv against the docx rules (regress when strictly greater than baseline*1.25 for loading time, baseline*1.20 for memory, baseline+10pp for CPU; No baseline for the two 'not yet benchmarked' register rows) and all 44 Results in solution/artifact_plan.json match, including the documented boundary cases (margaret-young/scribe-ml#8 CPU 90 vs 80+10 and amandagarcia/data-wizard#2 CPU 89 both Within tolerance; GitLab/eco-tracker#1 memory 841 vs 844.8 Within tolerance; dorothygonzalez/birdsong-analyzer#6 loading 30 vs 24*1.25=30 not a regression but CPU 98>85 is). layer1_realism_leakage__authoritative_re.explanation: The only authorities that drive the expected answer are the two supplied documents, both present and readable at /workspace/provided (baked in by the Dockerfile COPY provided/). The docx scope clause (open, performance-labelled, register repositories only), the metric-extraction clause ('take the number as written') and the tolerance clause are all consistent with the gold SQL recorded in consistency/attestation.json and with the csv's own 'Release benchmarked' column. layer1_realism_leakage__workflow_realism.explanation: Reading open performance-labelled issues across a benchmark register, applying a written tolerance policy against last-release baselines, logging one tracker issue per regression and producing a triage spreadsheet plus a one-page meeting summary is a realistic engineering-quality workflow with genuine user value. Access assumptions are satisfiable: the agent acts as susanthomas through the github-gym MCP tools used by the golden path (gh_issue_list, create_issue), and every figure it needs exists in the issue bodies or the provided csv. No contrived traps; the boundary cases are ordinary policy edge cases, not gotchas.

layer1_realism_leakage__golden_isolation.explanation: solution/ is never copied into the image (the Dockerfile COPYs only _app/task.toml, _app/instruction.md, _app/tests/ and provided/), /app is chmod -R go-rwx and the agent runs as rlgymagent (task.toml [agent] user), so manifest.json, rubric.toml and expected_diff.json are unreadable off disk. /logs/verifier is root:root 0700, created before the agent exists and guarded against symlink pre-creation in entrypoint.sh. Gym state is locked (/gyms 710 root:gym, mcp_databases chowned gym:gym go-rwx) and the gym access token lives only in root-readable task.toml, injected by the proxy. The agent-writable /workspace/provided copy cannot influence grading: _spec_paths_under_input rejects verifier specs that read seeded inputs, and the trusted input root is the root-owned /app/provided.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static.explanation: Aggregate fails because two mandatory subchecks fail — semantic_equivalence and surface_form_brittleness — on the same defect: the 16 regex matchers in summary_repository_lines (weight 0.18, pass_threshold 1.0) reject a semantically identical repository line whose counts are labelled in prose. Every other subcheck passes (traceability, depth, routing, execution completeness, bucket activation, aggregation, proportionality, independence, counterfactual strength, process grading), but a broad 0.82 score must not hide this specific defect.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__require.explanation: Each of the 8 requirement_ids in tests/manifest.json maps to an instruction span (consistency/requirements.json records the verbatim spans) and each instruction obligation has a check: xlsx population/figures/results (reports_register), PDF repository lines (summary_repository_lines), one page (summary_one_page), the three reserved totals (summary_total_*), the 20 tracker issues (20 flag_* database_state verifiers) and the 'write nothing else' constraint (nothing_written_beyond_the_regression_log). No reward-bearing verifier-only requirement and no material ungraded requirement (only the PDF 'title' is ungraded, which is immaterial).

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__coverag.explanation: Assertions are field-level, not existence-level. reports_register locks the exact 44-row population (row_set) with stop_at_blank_row false, then asserts the Result string for all 44 rows and all 132 numeric figures (numeric_tolerance 0.005). summary_repository_lines asserts 15 specific repository/covered/regression triples plus a population lock requiring exactly 15 such lines. The totals use pdf.find_labeled_value and assert the value, that there are no hedged alternatives, and that every occurrence agrees. The 20 flag_* SQL checks require exactly one issue with the exact lowercased title in repository 392 by user 17, no other entry for that repository, and at most 22 new entries. consistency/mutations.json records that blanking a figure, dropping a row, adding a row, or shifting every figure by one each fail the verifier that grades them. An empty or materially wrong deliverable cannot pass.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__evidenc.explanation: Artifact requirements are read from the artifacts: xlsx.read_rows on performance_triage.xlsx sheet Reports and pdf.extract_text / find_labeled_value / inspect_document on regression_summary.pdf, resolved against the real workspace by _run_file_check (which fails loudly rather than silently scoring 0 when the directory is missing). Side-effect requirements are read from the gym database by SQL through the proxy, not from the trajectory. No check reads trajectory data for an artifact requirement or vice versa, and no lossy conversion stands between a requirement and its evidence.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__semanti.explanation: Most of the grading is equivalence-tolerant — table_equals casefolds and whitespace-collapses text, parses numbers across '$', ',', ' ' grouping and trailing zeros, the id_pattern strips leading/trailing punctuation, and the issue-title SQL uses lower(trim(title)) so 'GitLab/...' vs 'gitlab/...' both pass. The exception is the PDF repository lines: a materially equivalent prose rendering is rejected. Concretely, against the gold pattern for row_gitlab_eco_tracker, 'GitLab/eco-tracker: 2 covered, 1 regression' and 'GitLab/eco-tracker - 2 reports covered, 1 regression' both fail while 'GitLab/eco-tracker | 2 | 1' passes, and repository_row_population would then count 0 of its required 15 matches, so the whole 0.18 bucket is lost. instruction.md does not explicitly require bare adjacent numerals for these lines.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__surface.explanation: The 16 lexical matchers in summary_repository_lines are the defect. Their separator class [\s|,;:/·•\-–—]+ tolerates pipes, commas, dashes, bullets, line wraps and letter-spacing (the names are spelled with \s* between every character, which is good), and the (?i) flag makes 'gitlab/eco-tracker' acceptable — but any word between the repository name and a count, or between the two counts, breaks the match. I verified this directly on the manifest regexes. The repository_row_population matcher compounds it: it is anchored \A...\Z and demands exactly 15 occurrences of the generic pattern, so a labelled rendering yields zero and fails too. Nothing in instruction.md discloses this; by contrast the three totals, where an exact label IS required, are explicitly spelled out in the instruction. The totals' find_labeled_value reader and the xlsx table_equals comparators are otherwise appropriately tolerant, and no matcher can be passed by mimicking tokens without the correct values.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__verifie.explanation: tests/test.sh -> tests/test_gvs.sh -> tests/test_outputs.py main(); engine_enabled is true via allowed_verifier_types, so _emit_engine_owned_reward runs every manifest verifier_config through the vendored VerifierEngine. evaluations/oracle/verifier/verifier_summary.json records total 27, passed 27, unscored 0 — no skipped, unreachable or silently failed check. Infrastructure failures are not laundered into zeros: _emit_engine_owned_reward raises RuntimeError on block.error or failure_mode == 'verifier_error' so the trial is recorded unscored, and _run_file_check returns an explicit error (not a silent 0) when the workspace is absent. No undeclared executable check exists.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__score_b.explanation: All 27 buckets carry non-zero weight and all 27 received evidence and passed in the oracle run (evaluations/oracle/verifier/verifier_summary.json). Weights sum to 1.0 (0.18 + 0.18 + 3x0.071111 + 0.023704 + 20x0.011852 + 0.165923). The disabled axes are reported honestly rather than presented as coverage: reward.json/verifier_summary.json record state.enabled false and sql.enabled false, and the rubric block carries mode 'benchmark' with the engine's own per-verifier items. tests/rubric.toml contributes zero rubric_check verifiers by design, and that is not counted as active coverage anywhere.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__aggrega.explanation: scoring.flat_verifier_scoring is true, so run_benchmark_verifiers computes passed_weight/total_weight pooled across all 27 items with per-item score 1.0/0.0 at the config's pass_threshold. Recomputing: all pass -> 1.0, which matches evaluations/oracle/verifier/reward.txt (1.0) and scored_weighted_pass_rate 1.0; losing summary_repository_lines alone -> 0.82; losing one flag_* alone -> 0.9881. The declared per-config weights are exactly the effective math. The manifest's scoring.weights (state 0, sql 0, rubric 1, trajectory 0) and side_effect_gate are inert in engine mode but cannot change the result, since the state axis is disabled (state_snapshot_enabled=false, expected_diff.json is {}) and hard_gate would be 1.0 regardless.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__scoring.explanation: Weight tracks materiality: the xlsx register (0.18) and the PDF repository breakdown (0.18) are the two largest analytic deliverables; the 20 tracker write-backs carry 0.237 in aggregate (0.011852 each, so one miss costs ~1.2%); the three totals carry 0.213; the no-extraneous-writes constraint carries 0.166. The purely cosmetic one-page check is the smallest bucket at 0.0237, so presentation cannot dominate. A fatal omission is not masked: an empty workspace fails all six file_checks (0.527) and writing nothing fails all 21 DB checks.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__check_i.explanation: The three sub-verifiers inside reports_register (population, results, figures) sit within one weighted config at pass_threshold 1.0, so they are one scoring decision, not three. The one genuine coupling is deliberate and disclosed in the config's own description: nothing_written_beyond_the_regression_log returns -1 (failing) until all 20 correct entries exist, so an agent missing a regression loses both that flag and the 0.166 bucket. The justification is sound and stated — without the completeness gate a do-nothing agent would harvest the largest single bucket for free, since 'wrote nothing extra' is trivially true of an agent that wrote nothing. Beyond that, each flag_* check predicates on a distinct issue title and the file_checks read disjoint assertions.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__counter.explanation: The package carries concrete acceptance cases in consistency/mutations.json run through this bundle's own specs: positive (oracle artifacts score 6/6 file_checks), semantic (one corrupted xlsx cell fails exactly reports_register), granularity (one corrupted value fails exactly one verifier, reward drops by its weight rather than to zero), incompleteness (blanking each total fails exactly its summary_total_* verifier; dropping the last Reports row fails reports_register), adversarial (a superset Reports sheet and an every-figure-off-by-one sheet both fail; a PDF padded with 40 non-answers fails summary_one_page), and a held-out rendering (libreoffice_pdf_from_docx) still passes. On the DB side the exact-title + population-cap SQL distinguishes a correct 20-issue write-back from a near-miss. The verifier can separate a genuine solution from a plausible defective one.

layer5_verifier_fairness_static__process.explanation: Reward depends only on the requested outcomes: the two workspace files and the GitHub end state. No verifier reads the trajectory, no narration is scored, and manifest.trajectory.scoring_per_step is never applied (trajectory weight 0; the engine path owns the entire score).
